meta.title_plain: How to design a game that's actually fun
meta.teaser: Learn the secret loops, rewards and difficulty tricks behind games you can't put down.

page.title: How to design a game that's actually fun
page.sub: A skill you can use today
page.bigIdea: Fun isn't luck. Game designers build it on purpose, with a loop you love to repeat and a challenge that grows with you.

cards.title: Find your core loop
cards.front: Every great game has one action you repeat forever.
cards.back: Roblox's creator guide calls it the core loop: the central gameplay a whole game is built on. An adventure game's loop might be explore, fight, upgrade, repeat.
cards.tryit: Pick a game you love, like Brawl Stars. Write its loop in 3 words. What do you do again and again?

cards.title: Teach without any words
cards.front: How did Mario teach millions of kids with no instructions?
cards.back: Shigeru Miyamoto built World 1-1 as a hidden tutorial in 1985. A slow first Goomba teaches jumping. A block gives a coin, so you try more blocks.
cards.tryit: Play the first minute of any game. List 3 things it taught you without saying a word.

cards.title: Reward progress, not just wins
cards.front: Why do you always want one more match?
cards.back: The progression engine moves you forward with new skills, levels or items. Roblox's guide warns that without it, a game feels repetitive, boring and shallow.
cards.tryit: Think of a game you quit. Write one reward that might have kept you playing.

cards.title: Balance the difficulty
cards.front: Too easy is boring. Too hard is stressful. So what's fun?
cards.back: Psychologist Mihály Csíkszentmihályi named the sweet spot flow. Challenge matches your skill, so you lose track of time. Like a tennis rally against someone your level.
cards.tryit: Remember a match where time flew by. Was your opponent easier, harder or just right?

cards.title: Playtest, then fix it
cards.front: Designers never know if their game is fun until...
cards.back: Playtesting means letting real people play before release to find problems. Watch where players get stuck or bored, then change your design.
cards.tryit: Invent a tiny game with a ball or paper. Have one person play it while you just watch.

words.d: The main set of actions a player repeats throughout a game.
How a game moves you forward with new levels, skills or items.
Being so focused and happy in a task that time disappears.
The part of a game that teaches you how to play.
Letting people try a game early to find what needs fixing.

quiz.q: A game makes you explore, fight, then upgrade, over and over. What is that called?
quiz.hint: Think about the shape of something that keeps coming back to the start.
quiz.why: The core loop is the cycle of main actions a player repeats all game long.

quiz.q: Your game is so easy that your friend yawns. What should you change?
quiz.hint: Flow needs challenge and skill to match. Which one is too low here?
quiz.why: When challenge is lower than skill, players get bored, so the challenge should rise.

quiz.q: Why does World 1-1's first Goomba walk slowly toward Mario?
opts: The NES was too slow for fast enemies
To give new players time to learn jumping
quiz.hint: Remember: this level was secretly a tutorial.
quiz.why: Miyamoto made the first danger easy to spot so players learn to jump by trying.

quiz.q: You finished your first Roblox game. What's the smartest next step?
opts: Publish it and never change it
Watch a friend play it and note where they get stuck
Delete it and start a brand new game
quiz.hint: How do designers find problems they can't see themselves?
quiz.why: Playtesting shows real problems, because the designer already knows how everything works.
